_doc: MedSim Studio template for case wrist_trauma_001. Everything an instructor can choose is listed here; nothing here adds or changes clinical findings, results or scoring rules of the case. Hints and companion lines are generic good-practice prompts and non-clinical speech. Not reviewed by a clinician.
label: Wrist injury after a fall (adult walk-in)
summary: Alex, 28, walks in the day after falling off a bicycle with a painful right wrist. History, focused examination, investigations, wrist support fitting and a management plan.
brief_base: Alex, 28, is waiting to be seen. Take a history, examine the patient, and record your findings, suspected diagnosis and management plan in the notebook.

environments.brief: Setting: a quiet outpatient clinic room.
environments.setting_context: You are being seen in a quiet outpatient clinic room.

environments.label: Emergency department bay
environments.brief: Setting: a curtained bay in an emergency department.
environments.setting_context: You are being seen in a curtained bay of an emergency department. There is background noise from the department.

calm: Take your time, Alex. I'm right here.
I'll hold your bag, don't worry about it.
Just tell them what happened, like you told me.
anxious: Is it serious? Please tell me it's not serious.
Shouldn't someone more senior be looking at this?
Alex needs that hand for work. How long is this going to take?
Sorry. I'll let you work. I'm just worried.

teammate.name: Kim
teammate.arrival_line: Hi, I'm Kim, one of the nurses. Tell me what you need and I'll fetch it.
teammate.delivery_line: Here you go: {item}. It's on the tray.
teammate.context: A nurse called Kim has come in to help the student.

personalities.guided: Cooperative and talkative; answers fully when asked.
personalities.standard: Cooperative but slightly anxious; answers what is asked.
personalities.challenging: Tense and brief; answers only what is asked and needs to be put at ease.

learning_objectives.label: Take a focused injury history (mechanism, onset, location, severity, associated symptoms)
Introduce yourself, ask permission before examining and respond to the patient's pain
Examine the injured wrist systematically and compare with an uninjured area
Choose imaging and interpret what its result does and does not exclude
Make a safe plan when imaging is not available on site
Measure, choose and fit a wrist support, checking circulation and comfort
Keep communicating clearly with a worried companion and a noisy room

hints.text: Start by introducing yourself and asking what happened.
Before you touch the patient, ask for permission.
Examine more than one area: the sore part, the area next to it, and the uninjured side for comparison.
If an examination hurt, acknowledge it before you carry on.
Decide whether imaging would help, and think about what a normal result would and would not rule out.
There is no imaging here. Write down how and when the patient should get it.
Before fitting a support, check colour, feeling and movement in the fingers.
Measure before you choose a size.
After the last adjustment, ask how the support feels and re-check the fingers.
Write your findings, what you suspect, and your plan in the notebook, then submit.

demo_draft._doc: Offline stand-in for the AI drafting assistant (assist.py): hand-written, non-clinical, combined per choice. Used unless MEDSIM_LIVE_AI=1.

scenes.outpatient_clinic: A bright outpatient room with the blinds half down, a box of gloves on the counter and the hum of the air vent filling the gaps in conversation.
scenes.emergency_department: A curtained bay in a busy emergency department: monitors chime next door, trolleys rattle past and the curtain never quite closes.
scenes.community_clinic: A cramped consulting room in a small walk-in clinic, its thin door letting through the reception phone and names being called. Nothing can be scanned in this building, so every decision about what to send on rests with the student.

bystander.calm: {name} sits in the corner holding the coat and the bag, steady and quiet, ready to fill in a detail if asked.
bystander.anxious: {name} will not sit down, hovers by the couch and cuts in whenever there is a pause, so the consultation has to hold together around the interruptions.

pressure.guided: Coaching appears on its own, which makes this a good first run of the case.
pressure.standard: Coaching only comes when the student asks for it.
pressure.challenging: There is no coaching at all, and the student sets the pace and structure alone.

personalities.guided: Open and chatty, Alex fills silences, adds small asides and answers fully once asked; easy to warm up, a little embarrassed about the fuss.
personalities.standard: Polite but on edge, Alex answers what is asked in plain sentences, winces before speaking and relaxes noticeably when things are explained before they happen.
personalities.challenging: Guarded and clipped, Alex gives one-line answers, glances at the door, and only opens up after a calm introduction and a clear reason for each question.

calm: Do you want me to step out, or is it fine if I stay?
I've got your phone, Alex, don't worry about it.
Shall I tell them about the bike, or do you want to?
Take your time. We're not in a rush.
anxious: Sorry, can I just ask, how long is this going to take?
Everyone out there looks like they've been waiting for hours. Are you on your own today?
Can you say that again? I missed half of it with that phone ringing.
I'm not trying to get in the way. I'm just worried, that's all.
